summary.text: Keisha Lance Bottoms, a Democrat, won the November 3, 2026 election for governor of Georgia, defeating Rick Jackson, according to unofficial results, and is set to take office when the new term begins.

She is a former Atlanta mayor and Biden White House official whose campaign called for expanding Medicaid, lowering driving costs, a statewide affordable-housing trust fund, and repealing Georgia's abortion restrictions.

paragraphs.text: Bottoms earned a bachelor's degree from Florida A&M University and a law degree from Georgia State University, and worked as an attorney and a magistrate judge.
She was elected to the Atlanta City Council in 2009 and re-elected in 2013, representing District 11.
She served as Atlanta's 60th mayor from 2018 to 2022.
In June 2022 she joined the Biden administration as senior advisor and director of the White House Office of Public Engagement.
Keisha Lance Bottoms won the November 3, 2026 general election for governor with 54.3% of the vote to Rick Jackson's 45.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
